intro: Twenty-five checks, in the order they can kill the project. Work top to bottom: a failed check in Layer 1 is not fixed by a better structure in Layer 3. The fifteen stop conditions at the end are not risks to manage; they are reasons to stop and change the plan.
note: This is a reading aid, not a filing. Nothing here is saved to a server — the boxes use your browser's own storage and can be cleared at any time.

checks.text: You can name, in one sentence, the job the Chinese entity will do that cannot be done from abroad.
checks.note: Invoice locally, employ staff, hold a licence, receive RMB, hold a lease. If the answer is 'be present', a distributor or a service agreement is cheaper.

checks.text: Your first three customers are identifiable by name, not by segment.
checks.note: The company registration is the easy part. A named pipeline is what tells you the entity is worth its annual cost.

checks.text: You know which of your customers require a fapiao, and at what rate.
checks.note: A customer that needs a 13% fapiao cannot buy from a small-scale taxpayer at 1%. This single fact changes the vehicle and the VAT status.

checks.text: You have a first-year budget that survives the company earning nothing for six months.
checks.note: Registration, address, accounting, payroll, your own salary and buffer. Founders routinely budget the setup and not the first year.

checks.text: You have visited, or spent at least a month in, the city you intend to register in.
checks.note: Registration practice, address supply and banking are local. A city that looks cheap from abroad often is not, once the address and the adviser are priced in.

checks.text: You have looked up your exact activity on the current negative list, not a summary of it.
checks.note: The 2024 edition has 29 national items. The wording of each item matters more than the headline number.

checks.text: You know whether your activity needs a sector licence, and which authority issues it.
checks.note: Education, healthcare, travel, food, telecoms and finance each have their own regulator. The business licence does not imply the sector licence.

checks.text: You have confirmed that foreign ownership is permitted for that licensed activity in your city.
checks.note: Some licences are open nationally, some are pilot-only, and pilots change by city and by year. Ask the local authority, in writing.

checks.text: Your registered address is zoned and documented for the activity you will actually carry out.
checks.note: Restaurants, clinics, schools and factories are address-sensitive. A cheap office that cannot be licensed for the activity is the most common wasted year.

checks.text: You can describe your business without using a word that triggers a licence you do not have.
checks.note: 'Investment advice', 'legal services', 'medical', 'school', 'news', 'payment' — the scope and the marketing copy both count.

checks.text: You have compared WFOE, JV and representative office against what you need the entity to do.
checks.note: Not against which sounds most impressive. A JV without a partner who brings a licence or a customer is a WFOE with a hostage.

checks.text: You know who the legal representative will be, and what that person is personally exposed to.
checks.note: The legal representative signs for the company and carries compliance risk. A nominee legal representative is a dispute waiting to happen.

checks.text: You have decided whether a Hong Kong or offshore holding company is worth its annual cost.
checks.note: It helps with future financing, currency and exit; it adds audit and filing obligations and a layer every bank will ask about.

checks.text: You have read the articles of association, especially board composition, voting and share transfer.
checks.note: The registry's template articles are not neutral. They decide what happens when shareholders disagree, which is exactly when you cannot renegotiate.

checks.text: You know where the company seal, the bank token and the tax login will physically be kept, and who can use them.
checks.note: Control of the seal and the bank token is control of the company. This is the first thing a Chinese investor will ask about.

checks.text: Your registered capital is enough for the licence minimum and the first year, and no more.
checks.note: It is a five-year promise and a liability cap. A large number is not credibility; it is a deadline.

checks.text: You know how the capital will actually arrive: which bank, which account, which documents.
checks.note: Capital goes into the capital account with a foreign-exchange registration. Wiring it to a personal account creates a problem you cannot fix by bookkeeping.

checks.text: You have chosen small-scale or general VAT status deliberately, and your customers accept it.
checks.note: General taxpayer status lets you issue 6% or 13% fapiao and reclaim input VAT. Small-scale is simpler and cheaper until a large customer refuses the invoice.

checks.text: You can explain how profit leaves China, and what it costs at each step.
checks.note: CIT, statutory reserves, 10% withholding (or treaty rate), and the bank's documentation. Model it before the first profitable year, not after.

checks.text: Your accounting arrangement is a named person or firm with a monthly deliverable, not a favour.
checks.note: Bookkeeping, VAT filing, payroll and the annual audit. The cheapest bookkeeper who files nothing is the most expensive line on the sheet.

checks.text: You have a work permit plan for yourself and for any foreign hire.
checks.note: Degree, two years of experience, salary above the local threshold, and an employer with a tax record. The permit is tied to the employer, not to you.

checks.text: You know the all-in cost of your first employee, including social insurance and housing fund.
checks.note: Employer contributions commonly add 25–40% to gross salary. A hiring plan built on gross salary is wrong by a third.

checks.text: You have a written employment contract and a severance expectation for every hire.
checks.note: China is not at-will. Unlawful dismissal costs two months per year of service; a documented process is cheaper than a tribunal.

checks.text: You know every recurring filing and the month it falls due.
checks.note: Annual report by 30 June, CIT settlement by 31 May, monthly VAT and payroll. Missing one puts the company on a list that freezes the bank account.

checks.text: You have an exit plan, including what closure costs and how long it takes.
checks.note: Six to twelve months for a clean company. Abandonment is not an exit; the entity, the penalties and the legal representative's record survive.

stops.text: The activity is prohibited to foreign investment and your plan is a nominee shareholder or a VIE.
The licence you need is not available to a foreign-owned entity in your city, and no permitted structure exists.
You cannot name a single customer who will pay the Chinese entity.
Your only route to market is invoicing through a Chinese friend's company.
You are about to sign a lease before the environmental, fire or sector approval that the site depends on.
The registered address is a virtual address that the bank has already refused, or that no landlord will document.
The business depends on bringing client money through the company without a payment licence.
The registered capital you need for the licence is money you do not have and cannot raise within five years.
Your Chinese partner's contribution is 'relationships' with no contract, no valuation and no exit mechanism.
You plan to be the legal representative but will not live in China or employ a local manager with authority.
Your product handles personal data at a scale you have not mapped, and you have no data-compliance plan.
The only person who can operate the business is a foreign national who does not qualify for a work permit.
You are relying on a verbal assurance from an official that a licence 'will be fine'.
Your budget covers registration but not the first twelve months of losses.
You have not read the articles of association or the joint-venture contract you are about to sign.
